transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-28
Time: 15:30 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE); Priya Patel (Redwood SE); Camille Ortiz (Redwood SE - joined later); Liam Chen (Emerald Head of ML); Maya Alvarez (CTO); Noah Brooks (SRE); Sofia Park (Product); Alexei Ivanov (Data Scientist)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Emerald's model selection constraints — context length needs (multilingual receipts/returns), tool-calling for inventory lookup, and which deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) makes sense for their compliance and latency requirements.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan with Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick intro round?
[00:08] Liam: yeah hi Liam, head of ml at emerald, we run recommendation and some chat ops for customer support.
[00:12] Maya: Maya here, cto.
[00:15] Noah: Noah, SRE.
[00:17] Sofia: Sofia, product.
[00:19] Alexei: Alexei, data science.
[00:22] Priya: Priya from Redwood infra SE, i'll be digging into performance and deployment.
[00:26] Jordan: cool, agenda — model selector, context length, multilingual, tool-calls / APIs, security / private deployment questions, next steps. sound right?
[00:32] Maya: yes thanks.

[00:45] Jordan: high level — are you prototyping in-house models or evaluating open models? what does current stack look like?
[00:52] Liam: We're mostly using a mix: embeddings with open-source SBERT variants and for generation we've been experimenting with Llama 2 forks from various vendors. but latency and cost are getting messy; also we need longer context for receipts and chat history, some docs are up to 50k tokens.
[01:10] Alexei: yep, we have multi-lingual customers, spanish and portuguese primarily then french. model quality drops on those for some of the smaller open models.

[01:25] Priya: got it. so a couple dimensions matter: context window (you said ~50k), multilingual quality, and tool-calling. what are your SLOs for p95 latency on support flows?
[01:36] Noah: we want under 600ms p95 for single-shot generation for responses that don't require heavy context; but for long-doc summarizations we can tolerate higher latency — up to 2s p95.
[01:48] Liam: cost target is also important. we can't blow the budget on an always-on 64k model for all routes.

[02:00] Jordan: that's common. Redwood can route lower-latency requests to faster quantized model variants and route heavy-context or high-accuracy requests to larger configs. question — are you okay with a hybrid approach (Hosted for most, Dedicated or Private for sensitive/high-volume flows)?
[02:14] Maya: yes, hybrid looks promising; but we need clarity around data residency, audit logs, and KMS. also we have vendor restrictions for PCI adjacent data so Private might be required for some flows.

[02:30] Priya: noted. on the model side: do you need tool-calling like inventory lookups, price checks with external APIs? or is it purely LLM outputs?
[02:40] Sofia: yes tool-calling. we want the model to call an internal inventory API to return stock counts and to call a pricing service for promotions. must be deterministic and auditable.
[02:50] Priya: Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output to make calls auditable; we also have invocation logs per request with token visibility — useful for debugging and for compliance teams.

[03:05] Jordan: any compliance certs you need specifically? SOC 2? ISO? region residency?
[03:10] Maya: SOC 2 is baseline, and we also need export controls documentation. some customers in EU require data to stay in-region.
[03:18] Jordan: Redwood has SOC 2 and ISO paperwork, we also have region controls for Dedicated and Private where you can keep data in specific cloud region or VPC. i'll share the security pack after this call.

[03:35] Alexei: on model selection, do you have benchmarks for multilingual performance and long context? we found Llama-2-70b quantized drops a lot for spanish when prompting.
[03:44] Priya: yes, we maintain a model catalog with perf profiles — quality vs latency vs cost. for multilingual we often see models trained with multilingual datasets (Mistral variants, BLOOM, or some Llama-2-multilingual forks) perform better. for long context, we have tested 32k and 64k context variants; they behave differently depending on attention implementation. we'll share the spreadsheet.

[04:05] Liam: curious what you recommend for 50k token docs — do we need a specialized 64k model or can we chunk + KV cache?
[04:14] Priya: two approaches: 1) use a native long-context model (64k) for single-pass summaries — simplest but more expensive; 2) use prefix-KV caching + chunking with a retriever layer and summarization pipeline — cheaper and often better for QA and retrieval + generation flows. depends on your latency and cost SLOs.

[04:35] Noah: can KV cache be used across concurrent sessions?
[04:39] Priya: yes, Redwood's runtime supports shared KV cache for hot prefixes and conversation history which helps cost on repeated patterns. it's configurable per-route.

[05:00] Jordan: talk about deployment tradeoffs — Hosted API is fastest to productize; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; Private gives you complete control (VPC, on-prem). what's most important?
[05:12] Maya: for most customer-facing chat it's okay to be Hosted as long as we can get logs and KMS integration. for payment-related flows and PII we want Private or Dedicated with VPC peering.
[05:24] Jordan: that aligns with hybrid routing — Redwood can tag routes and route based on policy.

[05:34] Sofia: any differences in model variants available across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[05:38] Priya: small differences: Hosted has the full catalog (including experimental builds) and Redwood-managed quantization. Dedicated typically has the curated production models we pre-validate; Private supports most model variants but some vendor-managed experimental builds may not be included by default — we can onboard models for Private but there's a lead time.

[06:00] Liam: what's the typical lead time to onboard a new open model to Private?
[06:04] Camille: usually 2-4 weeks depending on complexity (quantization, kernel tuning, sequence length support), sometimes faster if it's standard.

[06:18] Alexei: and for multilingual performance testing, can you run evals on our in-house datasets?
[06:22] Priya: yes, we can run eval jobs on Dedicated or Private. for Hosted we have sandboxed eval infra but for large datasets Dedicated is best. we'll need sample data — please scrub PII unless you want the Private route for that.

[06:40] Jordan: let's talk numbers — context sizes, throughput. do you expect large batch generation for offline processing?
[06:47] Liam: yes we do nightly batch summarization across a million documents truncated to variable lengths; that's more tolerant of latency but high throughput.

[06:55] Priya: Dedicated is ideal for high-throughput batch jobs with reserved capacity and autoscaling policies; Hosted can do burst but it's less predictable on cost/throughput.

[07:07] Noah: network egress — for Private we need to control egress, and apply NAT rules. can Redwood run in our VPC with egress controls?
[07:14] Priya: yes Private supports VPC deployment with customer-managed egress and HSM/KMS integrations for keys. we'll want to see your network diagram.

[07:28] Maya: tool-calling determinism — can we force the model to only return structured JSON and call our APIs ourselves? we want the app layer to own the side-effects.
[07:36] Priya: absolutely — function calling and structured schemas let you validate outputs. many customers use Redwood to get a structured payload, then their backend invokes the action. we provide traceability for each function call.

[07:50] Alexei: what about hallucinations? we've had models confidently invent SKUs. can Redwood do model routing to safer models?
[07:58] Priya: yes — policy-based routing can route high-risk prompts to more conservative models or heavier guardrails; and Redwood also supports reranking and verification steps against a vector DB to reduce hallucinations.

[08:12] Jordan: any budget constraints we should know?
[08:15] Liam: budget is approx $X/month for Hosted experiments, if it's significantly higher we'd need dedicated justification. for Dedicated we'd look at a reserved commit if unit economics make sense.

[08:25] Sofia: one more — multi-tenant isolation for models and keys? we need RBAC on who can deploy model versions and view logs.
[08:32] Priya: Redwood Console supports RBAC, SSO/SAML, and audit logs per token and per-route; Private gives you even stronger isolation with customer-managed control plane.

[08:45] Camille: quick note — we also support quantization profiles per workload; you can pick int8 for cheaper inference or int4/8 mixed strategies. that affects latency and quality.

[09:00] Maya: regarding int8 quantization, how much quality loss do you typically see for multilingual NLU use cases?
[09:06] Priya: it varies by model; for some 70B models int8 is minimal quality loss for generation but for nuanced multilingual understanding you might prefer int4/8 hybrid or keep FP16 on critical routes. we'll include per-model delta charts in the spreadsheet.

[09:25] Jordan: can you describe an example route mapping? like support-chat low-latency vs doc-summarization high-context?
[09:32] Priya: route A: support chat -> small/quantized 13B multilang model hosted for low latency. route B: doc summarization -> 64k variant on Dedicated/Private, or chunk+retriever pipeline on Hosted if cost constrained. route C: payments -> Private, restricted, model vetted + audit logging.

[09:55] Liam: good. about benchmarks: we need 8k, 32k, 64k comparisons and multilingual BLEU/chrF numbers. can you provide those?
[10:03] Priya: yes, we'll share our benchmark CSV and the raw eval harness. we'll run some quick jobs on your sample data if you share.

[10:17] Sofia: how do rollouts work? can we do canary deploys for model versions?
[10:22] Camille: Redwood supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies tied to quality/regression alerts. Console shows token-level cost and latency for each rollout.

[10:35] Noah: SLOs — if we buy Dedicated reserved capacity, do you offer latency SLAs?
[10:40] Jordan: yes Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; specifics in the contract.

[10:48] Alexei: curious about model provenance — can we see training metadata? especially for compliance with some customers.

[10:54] Priya: we include model provenance where available; for open models we surface upstream repo and known training corpora when published, but proprietary model vendors vary.

[11:05] Liam: any gotchas on using tool-calls with long contexts?
[11:09] Priya: nothing major — the only caveat is you need deterministic post-processing for calls. if you let model issue side-effects, include an idempotency layer. Redwood logs the function call payloads to assist debugging.

[11:22] Jordan: ok let's do a quick prioritization — what is your primary pilot use-case?
[11:26] Sofia: pilot of support chat with multilingual coverage and inventory tool-calls; secondary pilot is nightly doc summarization.

[11:33] Jordan: for the pilot i'd recommend Hosted for chat (fast to stand up) with route-level caching and a mid-sized multilingual model; if cost or residency becomes an issue we can move payment flows to Dedicated/Private.

[11:44] Maya: agreed. also we want to run a small benchmark for the 50k receipts to decide chunking vs 64k.

[11:53] Priya: action: we'll run a 50k doc summarization test on a 64k variant and on a chunk+retriever flow and share results.

[12:03] Liam: what would you need from us to get that going?
[12:07] Priya: sample dataset (scrubbed or Private), expected prompt templates, and target metrics (latency/cost/accuracy).

[12:15] Jordan: final recap and next steps — Jordan to send pricing and security pack, Priya to share benchmarks, Noah to share network diagram, Maya to confirm security call. any other blockers?

[12:26] Maya: no blockers.

[12:30] Jordan: great thanks everyone. Camille: want to pick up the technical deep dive and scheduling?

[12:35] Camille: yes i'll follow up with a calendar invite for week of Jan 12, timezone PT.

[12:40] Jordan: awesome thanks, meeting end.

References mentioned: security pack (link to security docs), benchmark spreadsheet (will be shared), model catalog.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had some mis-heard words (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'key cache' in a couple places) and speaker cuts around minute 6 when Camille joined.
